name: emlang-compositional
details: Complete implementation plan for Emlang Compositional - the next evolution of the emoji-based emergent language. This plan covers the addition of transformer emoji (higher-order operators), pattern matching, recursive definitions, semantic roles, and meta-linguistic operators to create a computationally complete visual language.

tasks.name: Phase1-Core
tasks.details: Maximum impact features: transformer emoji, basic pattern matching, and simple variable binding. These three additions provide the foundation for computational completeness.

sub_tasks.name: transformer-emoji
sub_tasks.details:
Implement transformer emoji as higher-order operators that transform other emoji.

Core transformers to implement:
- 🎭 Transform/Morph (state change)
- 🔄 Recursion/Loop (infinite iteration)
- 🧬 Pattern Replication (multiply patterns)
- 📦 Package/Encapsulate (defer evaluation)
- 🔗 Bind/Link (create relationships)
- ⚡ Force Evaluation (immediate execution)
- 🌀 Lazy/Suspend (thunk creation)
- 🪞 Reflection (meta-examination)

Each transformer needs grammar rules and feature unification logic.

sub_tasks.name: pattern-matching
sub_tasks.details:
Implement pattern matching with mathematical Unicode symbols.

Patterns to support:
- ⟨🔥|💧|💨⟩ (alternation)
- ⟨🔥,💧⟩ (sequence)
- ⟨🔥*⟩ (zero or more)
- ⟨🔥+⟩ (one or more)
- ⟨🔥?⟩ (optional)

Requires extending the parser to handle pattern syntax.

sub_tasks.name: pattern-syntax
sub_tasks.details:
✅ Pattern syntax fully implemented:
- Pattern delimiters: popen/pclose/por (word-based for tokenization reliability)
- Recursive alternation supporting unlimited elements
- Annotated elements in patterns
- Transformers on patterns (TransformedPattern)
- All integrated with compositional grammar

Examples working:
- popen 🔥 por 💧 pclose
- popen 💧 por 💨 por 🌍 por 🌑 pclose (unlimited!)
- 🔄 popen 🔥 por 💧 pclose (transformed pattern)
- popen 🌿 🔥 por 🧠 💧 pclose (annotated elements in pattern)

sub_tasks.name: matching-engine
sub_tasks.details:
✅ COMPLETE via pure .fgr grammar!

**Implementation**: Multiple productions + feature unification

Pattern[ can_match: fire ] -> ...
Pattern[ can_match: water ] -> ...

PatternMatch[ matched: #t ] -> Pattern[ can_match: #t ] MatchOp Element[ type: #t ]

Tag #t must unify → semantic type checking!

**Example**:
popen 🔥 por 💧 pclose matches 🔥 → ✅ (fire matches)
popen 🔥 pclose matches 💧 → ❌ 0 parses (fire ≠ water!)

See PARADIGM-SHIFT.md section 2.

sub_tasks.name: pattern-combinators
sub_tasks.details:
✅ COMPLETE via pure .fgr grammar!

**Implementation**: Pattern quantifiers bridge computational and ontological semantics:
- qstar (*) matches: zero, single element, PowerElement
- qplus (+) matches: single element, PowerElement (no zero!)
- qopt (?) matches: zero, single element (NO PowerElement!)

**Key Design**: Quantifiers match PowerElement structures!
- PowerElement[ base: #t ] unifies with pattern matches: #t
- PowerElement represents repeated manifestation (🔥🔥 = double fire)
- This maintains semantic coherence between syntax and meaning

**Grammar additions**:
- QuantStar/QuantPlus/QuantOpt terminals
- QuantifiedPattern rules with feature tracking
- QuantifiedMatch rules via multiple productions
- MatchZero operator for zero-count matches

**Tests**: 38/38 positive tests pass (100%)
- All elements (🔥 💧 💨 🌍 🌑)
- All quantifiers (qstar, qplus, qopt)
- Zero, one, and multiple matches
- Type unification working perfectly

**Semantic constraints enforced**:
- Type mismatches rejected (0 parses)
- qopt correctly excludes PowerElement matching
- Feature unification prevents invalid combinations

See tests-pattern-combinators.txt for comprehensive examples.

sub_tasks.name: variable-binding
sub_tasks.details:
✅ COMPLETE via pure .fgr grammar!

**Paradigm shift**: NO subscripts or lexer changes needed!

**Implementation**:
- Dynamic variables via word markers (x bind 🔥)
- Two-dimensional tag unification (#n = name, #v = value)
- 10 variable names: x, y, z, a, b, c, α, β, γ, δ
- Unlimited extensibility (just add Variable productions)
- Semantic checking via unification failure

**Example**:
x bind 🔥 arrow x → var: #0 x, val: #1 fire ✅
x bind 🔥 arrow y → 0 parses ❌ (semantic error!)

**Technique**: Feature tags propagate through parse tree = variable substitution!

See PARADIGM-SHIFT.md for full technical details.
